rubric_items.evidence: The verbatim first paragraph is declarative and precise: ‘A sampled main lobe can locate one isolated tone between bins, but denser FFT samples do not add observation time or separate unresolved components.’
Before the first general identity, the lesson computes a concrete fs=1024, N=64 analytic Hann tone, its 164.96 Hz frequency, 62.5 ms duration, 64 Hz lobe, and the 16 Hz versus 1 Hz grids.
Every section advances the one localization-versus-resolution decision: exact sampling identity, admissible local fit, window-dependent bias, phase failure, then the acquisition/interpolation ledger.

The chapter provides an exact theorem and proof, a scoped corollary and definition, a complete worked estimate, estimator boundaries, deterministic bias and phase studies, five explanatory visual roles, and six solved exercises.

The theorem now fixes N>=1, fs>0, acquired x[n], length-N w[n], and L>=N, and concludes only X_L[k]=X_w(e^{j2pi k/L}); duration and fixed-W lobe invariance are explicitly separated into ‘Corollary for the fixed acquisition and window.’ The definition is followed by canonical, structurally different, degenerate, and near-miss cases plus a generated-example Task.

The exercises mix computation, boundary diagnosis, refutation, derivation, strategy selection, prerequisite retrieval, and a seeded research-shaped experiment; the -12/0/-6 dB in-body exercise is parallel to the worked -6/0/-2 triplet.

The closed-book gate requires prior N/L, window-metric, transform-sign, and coherent-calibration knowledge; the strategy exercise later requires the reader to discriminate localization from resolution without prescribing one method.
All six Exercise blocks have complete Solution blocks with setup, algebra or reasoning, units, rejection clauses, and transferable conclusions; none is a trick or answer-only item.
Mechanical count is exactly one: the in-body three-bin dB interpolation warm-up. The other five require diagnosis, refutation, derivation, strategy choice, or reproducible simulation.

The set includes all four difficulty forms: bin/half-bin/zero/coincident boundaries, a plausible two-bumps claim to refute, a derivation of p and b skipped by the body, and a seeded 50-record research-shaped task.

Exactly one exercise reaches forward: the 50-record squared-magnitude task; its solution alone says a probabilistic estimator and averaging rule are required and includes Ref lesson=correlation-psd-and-welch.

Only one KeyFact remains: ‘The estimator report is incomplete without peak selection, signed curvature D, branch, transform scale, window calibration, amplitude-magnitude convention, and positive/negative-image isolation clauses.’ It synthesizes conditions developed across multiple paragraphs rather than restating one adjacent result. The two Asides supply hidden retrieval feedback and checkable source provenance.

The Smith Aside earns its inline pointer by identifying the controlled experiment being adapted, its changed formula/frequencies/peak rule, and the fact that the curves are regenerated; other citations remain in chapter-precise References.
A full prose scan found no ‘recreated below,’ ‘does the work,’ ‘under the hood,’ narration of notation already visible, or idiom-for-flavour.

The five visual roles are distinct: fixed-data versus longer observation, three-point fit geometry, window-dependent interpolation error, phase-created false maxima, and the claim-to-action ledger. Captions state the inference or task, and factual alt text is present.

Italics mark first-use terms, bold is limited to corollary/solution run-ins, inline code marks JavaScript output, and four em dashes over roughly 4.3k words remain below the density limit.
